turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr. Iyer, come and sit. You look worn out. Tell me, what is the problem today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor I am tired and this is irritating me no end. Since two days I am having a burning pain on the left side of the chest, and a few blisters have come up there.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Left side, burning, and blisters. When did it actually start?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, three days... no, two days. Day before yesterday, at night. I thought it was gas, then these blisters showed.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): The blisters came the same day as the pain?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Same time only. Four or five small ones. Burning like chilli on the skin. I have hardly slept, so I am snapping at everyone, sorry.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Don't worry about that. Does the pain cross over to the right side?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only the left. It stays in one strip. When the shirt rubs, it burns more.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough, cold, or difficulty in breathing?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough, no cold. Breathing is normal. Only this burning thing.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you lost weight recently?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I don't check.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, I will not mark that as weight loss. May I look at the chest?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, please be quick. I want to go and lie down.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): There is a small cluster of blisters, I count five, on a red base, left side of the chest, in a band. They are not crossing the midline.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): It is looking bad, no? Just give the tablets, doctor.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): One thing before the tablets. Did you have chickenpox when you were a child?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. As a child. Which year I cannot say, it is too long back. My mother said it was quite bad.

[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me summarise. Two days of burning pain with a few blisters, left chest only, no fever, no cough, and chickenpox in childhood. This is shingles, herpes zoster, along one nerve on the left. That is my working impression. I am not doing a test to confirm it today.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Shingles, at sixty-eight. Fine. What do I have to swallow?

[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will start you today itself on famciclovir, two hundred and fifty milligrams... no, sorry, not that. Acivlovir, eight hundred milligrams, five times a day, for seven days, by mouth.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Five times? My whole day will be tablets. Err. Alright, if I must.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Take them with a little food, not on an empty stomach. For the pain, paracetemol one gram, up to three times a day, if you need it.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): If I need it. I don't want extra tablets unless the burning is too much.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergy. I have swallowed so many tablets, nothing ever happened.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Who all is staying in the house with you?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): My wife, my son, and his wife. She is pregnant, six months, she is in the same house only.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then please listen. Fluid from these blisters can pass chickenpox to someone who never had it, and pregnancy is a real concern. Keep the rash covered. Do not let her touch it. No shared towels. Wash your hands. Avoid close contact with her until the blisters dry and crust.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): She will make a face. But I will cover it. I am too tired to fight.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): On the family side, any sugar, pressure, or heart trouble in the relatives?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar. My brother is in Pune, he is fine, nothing.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): And your own day, the job, the hours, food, exercise, alcohol?

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I am a retired post office clerk. I used to do eight hours, now maybe two hours helping my son with his shop bills. Diet is normal, rice and sambar, not too oily. Exercise, I walk twenty minutes in the morning, that is all. Alcohol I don't take, I stopped ten years back. No smoking also, I never smoked.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): So, retired post office clerk, now maybe two hours on your son's bills, rice and sambar, a twenty minute morning walk, alcohol stopped for ten years, never smoked. Have I got that right?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Correct. Can we close, my head is... no, not a headache, I am just fed up and I want my bed.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not sending any blood test or a swab. The rash is typical enough.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. I don't want extra poking. When do I come back?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come and see me in one week, even if the blisters are drying, so I can check them again.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): One week. If I must, I will drag myself. What else?

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the rash spreads towards the eye, or you feel very unwell, do not wait for that week, come the same day. Otherwise I will see you in one week. Keep it covered on the way home.

spec.situation: Older person with burning pain on one side of the chest and a few blisters for two days; remembers chickenpox as a child; doctor prescribes antiviral today and gives infection advice about contact with a pregnant relative.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

omissions.text: Pain/rash stayed only on the left and did not cross to the right side; it stayed in one strip/band and the shirt rubbing made the burning worse.
Blisters started at the same time as the pain, with about four or five small blisters.
Weight loss was asked about and not confirmed; doctor explicitly said he would not mark weight loss.
Paracetamol 1 g up to three times a day if needed for pain was prescribed/planned, not just counselling.
Doctor stated no confirmatory testing would be done today, specifically no blood test and no swab because the rash was typical enough.
